--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_cover()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check whether a collection of node groups covers every node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_cover()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Check whether a collection of node groups covers every node. title: >- [Graph.is_cover()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Check whether a collection of node groups covers every node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check whether a collection of node groups covers every node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46043-L46129){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_cover(communities) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is cover](../assets/graphs/is-cover.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles, A, B, C and C, D, E, sharing node C. Left: the groups A, B, C (teal) and C, D, E (violet) overlap at C and between them contain every node, so is_cover() returns True. Right: the groups A, B, C and C, D leave E out (in the accent color), so is_cover() returns False." width="100%"} A *cover* is a collection of node groups such that every node belongs to at least one group. Unlike a partition, the groups may overlap, as in the output of `cmty_k_clique()` or other overlapping community methods. Use this to check a collection before scoring it with `overlapping_modularity()`. Nodes in the groups that are not in the graph are ignored, matching NetworkX's `community.is_cover()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [communities]{.doc-parameter-name} : A list of node groups, each a list or set of node IDs or labels. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if every node of the graph is in at least one group. An empty graph is covered by any collection. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~cmty_k_clique`) : Overlapping communities that need not be a cover. [](`~overlapping_modularity`) : Score a cover. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles share node C. Overlapping groups that reach every node form a cover, and dropping a node breaks it: ::: {#38c1e34d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "C"), ]) ( graph.is_cover([["A", "B", "C"], ["C", "D", "E"]]), graph.is_cover([["A", "B", "C"], ["C", "D"]]), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: ### Clique percolation leaves members out `cmty_k_clique()` builds communities out of cliques, so a node in no clique of size `k` is in no community. On `karate_club()` with `k=3`, the communities are not a cover: ::: {#9354bfa1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() cover = karate.cmty_k_clique(3) karate.is_cover(cover) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: The two members left out, 9 and 11, drawn larger, are in no triangle: ::: {#3c5a6db5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} covered = set().union(*cover) missing = [n for n in karate.get_node_ids() if n not in covered] karate.plot(highlight=missing, label_by="label", seed=3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Adding each of them as a community of its own makes a cover, which `overlapping_modularity()` can then score: ::: {#0d4ac4c7 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.is_cover(cover + [[n] for n in missing]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: :::
